about: Local overlay on IHH's admission criteria for the Packet Triage tool. Adds fields only; rule text stays in the source file. Not an IHH document.

fields.kind: must | exclude | document | conditional | ask | note | eligible_condition | any_of. 'kind_source: overlay' means the source had no kind and the overlay inferred it from the list the rule sits in.
fields.needs_date: True if the check depends on a date or time window. Dates are redacted, so return 'can't tell' unless timing is stated without a date.
fields.gap: True if IHH's written rules leave this unclear or a settled conflict applies. Show gap_note to the coordinator; never decide silently.
fields.evidence: Where the evidence usually is (DOC-n from IHH's referral checklist, or a page type).
fields.facts: Which of the 27 core facts the rule depends on.

fact_keys.wounds: Wounds: location, size, stage, who does care
fact_keys.vitals_last5: Last 5 sets of vital signs stable
fact_keys.mental_health_stable: Mental health diagnosis; stable on meds

global_notes: Outcomes are approve or deny; there is no stated 're-refer when ready' for a patient who will qualify in a day or two.
When the referral form (FORM-*) and the outline disagree, the outline wins. Where the outline is silent, the form's exclusion applies.
Dates are redacted in the packets: rules with needs_date=true should return 'can't tell' unless the packet states the timing without a date.
Ophthalmology has no ineligible conditions listed in the source. Treat that as 'none listed', not 'nothing excludes'.

rules.text: Homeless/at risk of homelessness and too ill or frail to recover from illness or injury
Lives alone with no formal supports and too ill or frail to recover from illness or injury
At risk of hospitalization or re-hospitalization after hospitalization
Able to complete all Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) independently including personal hygiene

Patient must be able to complete personal hygiene independently. Benches are available for bathing so seated shower is acceptable. Patient must be able to gather all of their own bathing/showering supplies, transfer to shower area and perform shower/bath independently
Able to toilet independently and/or change briefs/diapers independently
If using DME (wheelchair, walker, etc) must be able to use independently
PT/OT notes must be sent for review
Patient must be able to ambulate at least 100 ft (rest breaks are acceptable) at modified independence if not wheelchair dependent
rules.gap_note: Settled: wheelchair-dependent patients who transfer and use the chair independently are eligible.

rules.text: Wheelchair dependent patients must be able to transfer independently
rules.gap_note: Settled: see MOB-3.

rules.text: Patient must be mentally stable on medications
No suicidal ideation
No commanding auditory or visual hallucinations

If a patient was admitted with acute alcohol intoxication, the patient must be held for at least 72 hours and not have signs of alcohol withdrawal (maintain a CIWA-AR score of <8, if being assessed with this tool) prior to admission to recuperative care.
Cannot qualify, have history of or currently be under a conservatorship or FSP
rules.gap_note: 'FSP' is not spelled out; likely Full Service Partnership, a county mental-health program.

rules.text: Must be capable of self-administering medications (must confirm that patient can self-administer insulin) and receiving medical education
AOx4
Ineligible if client is verbally or physically aggressive towards staff or other patients
Patients that are registered sex offenders will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis (however, as a general guide, any offense that involves violence will likely be denied
rules.gap_note: Settled: case by case; offenses involving violence likely denied. Flag for the coordinator; never auto-deny.

rules.text: Patients with IV access can be accepted if they have home health established to maintain the IV and administer the medication as needed. There is no limit on time for IV
rules.gap_note: Home health threshold wording varies across rules: established, ordered, coordinated, coordinated and scheduled.

rules.text: Cannot accept patients on isolation unless isolation status is cleared prior to admission to recuperative care

Hospice patients are eligible for recuperative care admission. Hospice services must be arranged prior to admission to recuperative care and patient, family and other involved parties must be made aware that recuperative care staff cannot administer medications, these medications will be administered by hospice staff
MRSA swab, documented negative prior to recuperative care admission if coming from inpatient hospitalization
Covid swab (rapid swab acceptable) documented negative within 24 hours of recuperative care admission if coming from inpatient admission
rules.date_note: COVID swab negative within 24 hours of admission
rules.gap_note: A swab negative when the referral is sent can be more than 24 hours old by arrival.

rules.text: If patient is being referred from inpatient hospitalization, 5 consecutive glucose readings should be sent. Readings must be show improvement and stabilization.
If admitted from the emergency department, it must be established and documented that the patient is not in DKA.
rules.gap_note: Related to END-X3: resolved DKA not addressed.

rules.text: We will not accept a diabetic patient that was started on an insulin regimen less than 24 hours prior to admission.
rules.date_note: Insulin regimen started less than 24 hours before admission
rules.gap_note: Does not say whether the 24 hours start at the first dose or when doses stop changing.

rules.text: Poorly controlled diabetics on an oral medication or established insulin regimen may be accepted from the ED if they have follow up with a primary care provider scheduled within the next 5-7 days, have not had an episode of hypoglycemia within the last week and have a written treatment plan for glucose control (i.e. sliding scale parameters, medication hold guidelines, etc).
rules.date_note: Follow-up within 5-7 days; no hypoglycemia in the last week

rules.text: Patient should understand how to use glucometer
Patient should understand insulin administration, if applicable
Does the patient use insulin? Is the insulin administered through a pump?
Does the patient take oral medication?
What was the patient's last hemoglobin A1C? This is not a limiting factor for admission but does provide important information about the patient's baseline glucose level
rules.gap_note: The A1C sentence is cut off in the source.

rules.text: The last 5 sets of vital signs should be sent. Patient is ineligible for recuperative care if VS show signs of sepsis (continued fever, elevated heart rate, low blood pressure)
The patient should be able to administer oral antibiotics independently
If IV antibiotics are required, home health care should be ordered before admission to recuperative care to maintain IV and administer antibiotics
rules.gap_note: Home health wording varies (see OTH-3).

rules.text: Location of infection?
Were cultures performed? Results should be sent
Is the patient on isolation?
Chest imaging should be sent (Chest XR, CT, MRI) when available

The last 5 sets of vital signs should be sent, if available; O2 saturation may be chronically low if patient has a history of COPD, readings should be stable and consistent with patient's normal O2 saturation
If O2 is required, the hospital must order it and have the tank ready to be sent to the site the day before the client arrives at the recuperative care site
rules.date_note: Oxygen tank ready the day before the client arrives

rules.text: Respiratory therapy notes should be sent
Is the patient receiving any breathing treatments? If so, what are they?
Is the patient on antibiotics for this condition?
The last 5 sets of vital signs should be sent. Patient's BP should be stable on oral medication for at least 24 hours
rules.date_note: Blood pressure stable on oral medication for at least 24 hours

rules.text: If patient had a troponin in the hospital, at least 3 consecutive results should be sent with at least 2 negative results
rules.gap_note: Asks for two negative troponins, but a patient admitted for a heart attack won't have them, while history of heart attack (CIR-E7) is eligible.

rules.text: EKG results should be sent

If patient has a history of atrial fibrillation or has been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation, patient should be able to take anticoagulation therapy independently and understand any associated lab work (i.e. INR) necessary to track this medication

Ejection Fraction of 25% or higher may be accepted as long as this has been established to be the patient's baseline. If the patient is on chemotherapy or is being immediately discharged from hospitalization for heart attack with a lowered ejection fraction, this patient is ineligible for recuperative care
Patient will not be accepted for admission to recuperative care if IV blood pressure medications have been required within 24 hours
rules.date_note: No IV blood pressure medicine within 24 hours

rules.text: Uncomplicated infections of the skin, cellulitis or abscess, requiring oral antibiotic treatments

Wound care to be coordinated with home health agency prior to arrival at recuperative care and should coincide with the frequency of dressing changes or wound monitoring. If a patient should have a dressing change or wound check within 24 hours of discharge from the hospital, wound care should be arranged to arrive to recuperative care within 24 hours. Additionally, all wounds in hard-to-reach areas (coccyx, back of thighs, back, perineum) will require at least one visit from wound care in the recuperative care setting regardless of patient's ability to change the dressing in a hospital setting.
rules.date_note: Wound care to arrive within 24 hours if a dressing change is due
rules.gap_note: Hard-to-reach list reads 'coccyx, , back of thighs, back, perineum': an item seems missing and the sacrum is not named. Home health wording here is 'coordinated' (see OTH-3).

rules.text: IV antibiotics are allowed as long as home health has been coordinated to maintain the IV and either patient is able to administer their own IV antibiotics or home health will be administering the antibiotic
rules.gap_note: Home health wording varies (see OTH-3).

rules.text: Uncomplicated wounds (e.g. laceration without infection)
Post-surgical incision. If staples or external sutures are placed, appropriate follow up should be scheduled for removal prior to admission to recuperative care
Stage 1, 2, 3 pressure ulcers. Wound care to be coordinated and scheduled prior to admission to recuperative care
rules.gap_note: Home health wording varies: here wound care must be 'coordinated and scheduled' (see OTH-3).

rules.text: Third degree burns that affect <15% of the body. Wound care to be coordinated with home health agency prior to admission to recuperative care
rules.gap_note: Home health wording varies (see OTH-3).

rules.text: Complicated wounds requiring skin grafting
Complicated large abscess
rules.gap_note: 'Complicated large abscess' is not defined.

rules.gap_note: C. diff is ineligible; the outline does not say whether that ends when isolation lifts or when treatment finishes. The form (FORM-X4) excludes it only until cleared by a doctor or CID. Show both to the coordinator.

rules.text: Diabetes that shows improvement and stabilization in glucose levels as seen on at least 5 consecutive glucose readings with medical treatment (see the diabetes rules)
Hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism on medical treatment
s/p thyroidectomy

Alcoholic ketoacidosis

Urolithiasis

Post coronary artery bypass graft or heart valve surgery with controlled, stable blood pressure, normal hemoglobin/hematocrit, normal EF and without arrhythmias. Home health must be ordered and scheduled prior to admission to recuperative care. Cardiac surgery follow up must be scheduled prior to admission to recuperative care.

History of heart attack. If being admitted to recuperative care immediately following admission for heart attack, will only accept patients who have an normal ejection fraction

rules.gap_note: Only the tuberculosis part falls to the form (the outline is silent on TB). MRSA is covered by INF-1 and C. diff by GI-X3, so the outline governs those.
